overview.title: Visualizing the trained YOLO model's predictions
overview.section: 12.2 Training a YOLO model from scratch
overview.main_topic: Running the trained YOLO model on one validation image, converting its outputs (boxes and per-cell argmax labels) and drawing predictions above a confidence cutoff (Listing 12.13, figure 12.6)
overview.central_idea: After 4 epochs the model already places a plausible box around the giraffe and labels the right grid cells, but with only 0.16 confidence. A cutoff of 0.1 shows that one box; cutoff=None shows every box the model predicts (figure 12.7 on the next page).
overview.importance: This is the first look at what the from-scratch detector actually does. It shows how raw network outputs become a visual detection, and why the confidence threshold is a key knob when reading detector outputs.
learning_objectives: Explain how val_dataset.rebatch(1) yields a single sample
Describe the shapes of preds['box'] and preds['class'] and how argmax produces a per-cell label map
Explain what the cutoff argument of draw_prediction does, including cutoff=None
Interpret figure 12.6: what the model gets right and what the 0.16 confidence means
prerequisites: Model outputs: box (6, 6, 5) and class softmax (6, 6, 91) (p.362)

summary:
**Listing 12.13** (captioned, somewhat confusingly, "Training the YOLO model") inspects the trained model on one image:

1. `val_dataset.rebatch(1)` re-splits the validation batches of 16 into batches of 1, and `next(iter(...))` takes the first: an image tensor `x` of shape (1, 448, 448, 3) and its targets `y` (callout: *Rebatches our dataset to get a single sample instead of 16*).
2. `model.predict(x)` returns a dict; `preds["box"][0]` is the (6, 6, 5) box grid of that image.
3. `np.argmax(preds["class"][0], axis=-1)` turns the (6, 6, 91) softmax into a (6, 6) map of the most likely label per cell (callout: *Uses argmax to find the most likely label at each grid location*).
4. `path = metadata[0]["path"]`: because the validation set is the first 500 batches in metadata order, the first validation sample is `metadata[0]`. The original file is reloaded so the image can be viewed at full size (callout).
5. `draw_prediction(path, boxes, classes, cutoff=0.1)` shades grid cells by predicted class and draws only boxes with confidence at least 0.1.

**Figure 12.6** shows a giraffe among trees, overlaid with the 6 x 6 grid. A block of cells around the giraffe is shaded in one class color, and a single box labeled **"giraffe 0.16"** frames the animal reasonably well. The text concludes that the model is *starting to understand box locations and class labels, though it is still not very accurate*.

To see everything the model outputs, the page calls `draw_prediction(path, boxes, classes, cutoff=None)`, which draws **every** predicted box, even those with zero confidence; the result is figure 12.7 on p.370.

paragraphs.what_it_says: Listing 12.13 takes one validation sample, predicts on it, extracts the box grid and argmax class map, and draws predictions with confidence at least 0.1 on the original image.
paragraphs.what_it_means: Raw outputs need two post-processing steps before they are viewable: selecting the single image from the batch axis ([0]) and turning class probabilities into hard labels (argmax). The cutoff then filters boxes by confidence.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: This is the minimal inference-and-visualization loop for a grid detector; real detectors add non-max suppression and calibrated thresholds on top.
paragraphs.technical_idea: Each of the 36 cells always outputs a box; whether it is shown depends only on its confidence channel (index 4) versus the cutoff.

concepts.name: Confidence cutoff
concepts.definition: A threshold on a detector's confidence score; only predictions at or above it are reported.
concepts.intuition: A volume knob between 'show only what you're sure about' and 'show everything'.
concepts.technical: draw_prediction tests box[4] >= cutoff for each of the 6 x 6 cells; None disables filtering.
concepts.significance: Trades precision for recall; the book uses a low cutoff (0.1) because the model's confidences are low.
concepts.example: cutoff=0.1 shows the 'giraffe 0.16' box; cutoff=0.2 would show nothing for this image (inference from the figure).
concepts.misconception: A low confidence doesn't mean the box is wrong; here the box is plausible but confidence is low because training is incomplete.

concepts.name: Argmax decoding of class maps
concepts.definition: Turning per-cell class probability vectors into a single predicted label per cell by taking the index of the maximum.
concepts.intuition: Each cell votes for its most likely class.
concepts.technical: np.argmax over axis -1 of a (6, 6, 91) array gives (6, 6) integers.
concepts.significance: Produces the labels used to color cells and name boxes.
concepts.misconception: Argmax discards uncertainty; a cell at 30% giraffe and 29% zebra looks as certain as one at 99%.

concepts.name: Object detection
concepts.definition: Predicting bounding boxes and class labels for the objects in an image.
concepts.technical: Here a single-stage YOLO-style grid detector predicting one box per cell.
concepts.misconception: A detector's raw output is not a short list of objects; it is a fixed grid of candidates that must be filtered.

deeper.title: Reading 'giraffe 0.16'
deeper.body:
1. 'giraffe' is `coco_id_to_name(classes[yi, xi])` for the cell whose box passed the cutoff, i.e. the argmax label of that cell.
2. 0.16 is that cell's confidence output, `boxes[yi, xi, 4]`.
3. The loss trained confidence to match the IoU between the predicted and true box (p.367), so 0.16 is the model's own estimate that its box overlaps the truth with an IoU around 0.16.
4. Visually the box fits better than that, which (inference) suggests the confidence head is lagging behind the localization head after only 4 epochs.

deeper.title: From grid outputs to a final detection list
deeper.body: Beyond the book. Production grid detectors do more than threshold: they (1) multiply confidence by class probability to get class-specific scores, (2) drop scores below a threshold, and (3) apply **non-max suppression**, keeping the highest-scoring box and removing others that overlap it with IoU above, say, 0.5. The book's draw_prediction only performs step 2, which is enough here because the model predicts at most one box per cell.

visualizations.title: From model outputs to drawable predictions
visualizations.why: Listing 12.13 goes from one (1, 448, 448, 3) image to (6, 6, 5) boxes and a (6, 6) argmax label map.

questions.question: What does `val_dataset.rebatch(1)` do in Listing 12.13?
options: Re-splits the batches so each element holds a single sample
questions.answer: Re-splits the batches so each element holds a single sample
questions.explanation: The callout says it rebatches to get a single sample instead of 16. It doesn't shuffle, repeat or drop labels (y is still returned).

questions.question: What is the shape of `classes` after the argmax, and what does each entry represent?
questions.answer: (6, 6); each entry is the index of the most likely of the 91 COCO labels for that grid cell.
questions.explanation: preds['class'][0] is (6, 6, 91) and argmax over axis -1 removes the last axis.

questions.question: Why is `metadata[0]['path']` the correct image for the prediction?
questions.answer: Because val_dataset is dataset.take(500), the first batches in metadata order, so its first sample after rebatching is metadata[0].
questions.explanation: Listing 12.9 built the dataset from metadata in order and split validation off the front.

questions.question: In figure 12.6 the box is labeled 'giraffe 0.16'. What is 0.16?
options: The predicted confidence of that cell's box
The IoU with the true box measured on the validation set
questions.answer: The predicted confidence of that cell's box
questions.explanation: draw_prediction prints the box's confidence channel. It was trained toward IoU but is the model's prediction, not a measured IoU; the class probability is not printed.

questions.question: Why does the book use a cutoff of only 0.1?
questions.answer: Because the undertrained model outputs low confidences; a higher cutoff would hide even correct boxes.
questions.explanation: p.368 announces a low-confidence cutoff because the model is not a very good detector yet.

questions.question: Without looking, can you explain what happens inside draw_prediction when cutoff=None?
questions.answer: `not cutoff` is True, so the condition passes for every cell and all 36 boxes are drawn.
questions.explanation: This is the mechanism behind figure 12.7.
